title: The Wrong Widow

player_frame.role: Adjudicate competing Civil War widow’s pension claims from supplied county and military paper
player_frame.objective_player_facing: Two women claim the same soldier’s widow’s pension. Decide which claim the records can carry — and reconstruct what happened without treating any one document as gospel.

cold_open_rule: Stakes first. No county lore dump, regiment lecture, or how-to-research manual before the dual claim is felt.

opening_artifacts.why_first: Immediate dual-claim conflict — two widows, one soldier, both pending/contested.

opening_artifacts.why: Martha asserts 1858 Ripley marriage + wartime wartime death; names two children.
Lydia asserts 1866 Jefferson marriage + 1887 death; sincere belief first wife died of fever.
player_sees: told first wife died of fever

opening_artifacts.why: 1887 death register names Lydia — sets the primacy trap that Act IV must overturn via earlier marriage + no divorce.
opening_artifacts.design_note: Brief allowed muster OR death register as #4. Trail picks death register so cold open lands the primacy trap; war-paper split waits for Act II (D007/D008) as the escalating reveal.

not_in_opening: D005/D006 full registers (unlocked in Act I research)
first_research_ask: What does each woman assert, and can both marriages be verified as recorded events?
